issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named get_total_number_of_students() (with underscores) while the UML diagram and the provided solution use the camelCase name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This naming inconsistency between the textual description and the UML/solution can confuse students about the exact method name they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all materials. Update problem_statement.md to refer to getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase) to match the UML diagram and the template/solution, or alternatively change the UML and solution to use get_total_number_of_students() if underscores are preferred.

issues.description: The problem description uses the snake_case name get_total_number_of_students() while the UML in the same problem statement and the reference solution implement the method as getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual method (total number of students) can confuse students mapping the textual requirements to the Java implementation and tests, since Java conventions and the provided solution expect camelCase.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the naming across artifacts by updating problem_statement.md to use the camelCase method name getTotalNumberOfStudents() (matching the UML and Java conventions). Alternatively, if snake_case is intentional (not recommended for Java), update template and solution to match — but prefer using camelCase to avoid extra student confusion.
